grammar.title: Gramatyka
grammar.rule: Biała kartka. Ala widzi białą kartkę. Na białej kartce jest stary napis. Jan nie przesuwa złego stołu.
grammar.note_en:
An adjective describes a noun. Agreement means that its form matches the noun’s grammatical gender, number and case. This chapter stays singular: one object at a time. Case expresses the noun phrase’s job, such as a naming form, a direct object or a static place. Both the adjective and noun participate: the noun endings already introduced do not disappear when a description is added.

The naming, or nominative, forms show three genders. Stół is masculine, so czerwony stół means “a red table”; kartka is feminine, so biała kartka means “a white note/sheet”; pudełko is neuter, so małe pudełko means “a small box”. The familiar masculine mały / duży (“small / large”) now contrasts with małe / duże (“small / large”, neuter), and duża (“large”, feminine). Duża lampa means “a large lamp”; duże narzędzie means “a large tool”. These are grammatical genders, not a rule about an object’s physical size. The old table has not shrunk since chapter1: it is still large, but the lamp, cable, paper and tool leave insufficient working space. The new table offers a different arrangement rather than a taught comparative such as “larger”.

For a feminine affirmative direct object, -a becomes -ą in the adjective while the shown noun takes its accusative form: biała kartka → białą kartkę (“white note”, naming → object); luźna noga → luźną nogę (“loose leg”); cudza lampa → cudzą lampę (“lamp belonging to someone else”). Ala bierze białą kartkę means “Ala takes the white note”; Ala widzi luźną nogę means “Ala sees the loose leg”; Ewa says Widzę cudzą lampę, meaning “I see the lamp belonging to someone else”. The two endings need not be the same letter. Starą kopertę means “the old envelope” as an object. Do not write a nominative adjective before an accusative noun merely because the adjective’s meaning has stayed the same.

The masculine objects shown here are inanimate: a table or drawing. Their affirmative accusative forms match their naming forms: Jan przesuwa czerwony stół means “Jan moves the red table”. This is not a licence for personal or animate accusatives. Neuter objects also keep the same adjective and noun forms: małe pudełko / duże narzędzie means “small box / large tool”, in naming or affirmative object use. Every form collected in the first table has occurred in reading; the chapter does not introduce full forms for every adjective in every gender.

Negating an object-taking action still changes its direct object into the genitive, as in chapter3. The adjective changes too. Jan nie przesuwa złego stołu means “Jan does not move the bad table”. Zły → złego contrasts a masculine naming form with the masculine genitive. Stołu is the genitive of stół; this new surface form belongs to the already-known noun. Jan nie bierze nowego rysunku means “Jan does not take the new drawing”. Nie obraca luźnej nogi means “does not turn the loose leg”; luźna → luźnej is the feminine adjective change, alongside noga → nogi. Ala nie bierze cudzej lampy means “Ala does not take the lamp belonging to someone else”. Negative search still takes genitive too, but no new search government is introduced here. The table’s old / new / bad descriptions are not genitive ownership phrases.

Static w and na still name where something is, with the locative. Na starym stole means “on the old table”; na nowym stole “on the new table”; na czerwonym stole “on the red table”; na białym papierze “on the white paper”; w małym pudełku “in the small box”. The masculine and neuter locative adjective forms shown here end in -ym. Na białej kartce means “on the white note/sheet”: feminine locative has -ej in this pattern. The feminine adjective ending -ej occurs in both these locative and genitive patterns; that ending alone does not identify the case. Compare białej kartce, a static locative, with feminine genitive luźnej nogi or cudzej lampy. Learn the complete phrase and its governing construction. Papierze is the locative of papier; it is not a new word. No directional use of these prepositions is licensed by a static example. Taking and putting keep their earlier forms with tu/tam.

Dobry means “good”, zły “bad”, nowy “new”, stary “old”, czerwony “red”, biały “white”, luźny “loose”, and noga “leg”. The concrete scene gives each judgment its context: a large table can still be a bad choice when its leg is loose. New describes the newly introduced table or freshly drawn sheet, not a new tense. Stary napis is the old wording still visible on the inventory note: finding the lamp does not change Brak into a different inscription. Cudzy was first met receptively in chapter4. It becomes productive here only for the forms actually modelled: cudza, cudzą and cudzej. It means that the object belongs to someone else from the speaker’s perspective; it does not identify the lamp’s owner.

Potrzebny is an adjective meaning “needed”. Potrzebny jest duży stół means “A large table is needed”; Potrzebny jest stolarz means “A carpenter is needed”. The noun stolarz is the subject in its naming form, and potrzebny is an agreeing adjective. This is not a noun predicate in the instrumental, a personal direct object or a modal verb followed by an infinitive. Stolarz names the occupation generically; nobody arrives or speaks as a carpenter in this chapter. The forms shown make a need explicit while leaving the next action for the following chapter.

items.prompt: „Na stole”: co stoi na starym stole?
items.model_answer: Na starym stole stoi duża lampa.
items.rubric: Name the real upright lamp, not its paper drawing. Its cracked cable lies on the same original table. The old table is still the large table described in chapter1; the problem is inadequate usable workspace for this arrangement.

During section1 Ala takes the repair tool; she also handles the white inventory note and lamp drawing. Accept an accurate full sentence identifying a held object at an actual point, without claiming a lamp pickup.
Name the newly introduced red candidate table in a full sentence. The original worktable remains where it was and keeps supporting the lamp.
Name the loose leg Jan turns while inspecting the red table, not the whole original table or the lamp. The inspection discovers the fault; it does not repair it.
Accept the leg, the table, or both in a full sentence. This new blank sheet becomes a joint/table sketch; the old lamp drawing, chapter4 search sketch and old practice sheet remain separate.

items.prompt: „Potrzebny stolarz”: co leży na czerwonym stole?
items.model_answer: Na czerwonym stole leży nowy rysunek.
items.rubric: Only the new table/leg sketch lies on the red table at the end. The physical lamp stays upright on the old table; no repair or carpenter arrival has occurred.

Give a truthful complete first-person sentence using widzę and a taught object form. A canonical example is a white note or sheet, but no personal environment is assumed. A truthful negative such as Nie widzę białej kartki is also valid; use genitive after the negative object-taking verb.
